risks.note: Management notes the rapid acceleration in AI-led infrastructure demand has created supply-side pressures across select hardware categories: higher demand for servers, memory, storage and high-performance computing components has raised hardware and RAM prices, while tighter availability has extended procurement and delivery timelines. For a distribution/aggregation model this means longer lead times, pricing volatility and the need for proactive capacity planning in customer deployments.
risks.risk: Hardware supply-side pressure and component price inflation

risks.note: The Company positions itself as a 'vital link' that enables OEMs to reach enterprise customers by partnering with System Integrators. Revenue therefore depends on retaining OEM mandates and SI relationships rather than on owning the underlying technology, making partner retention and portfolio relevance a structural exposure.
risks.risk: Structural dependence on OEM and System Integrator ecosystem

risks.note: The MD&A states the pace of technological change is reshaping competitive dynamics; enterprise technology domains 'often have multiple products and solutions to choose from', so the portfolio must continuously be refreshed toward emerging OEMs and AI-era architectures to stay relevant.
risks.risk: Pace of technological change and shifting competitive dynamics

risks.note: Management notes that while sustained investment in digital technologies should support long-term productivity growth, global markets remain sensitive to shifts in technology valuations, capital allocation patterns and the broader economic environment — a moderation in enterprise AI/IT spend would flow directly into the Company's demand.
risks.risk: Sensitivity to technology valuations and enterprise capital-allocation cycles

risks.note: The outlook is described as increasingly complex amid heightened geopolitical tensions, trade fragmentation risks and persistent fiscal imbalances; commodity price volatility, supply chain reconfiguration and elevated policy uncertainty continue to challenge business confidence and investment planning.
risks.risk: Geopolitical tension, trade fragmentation and policy uncertainty

risks.note: Global trade disruptions, geopolitical tensions and commodity price volatility are stated to have contributed to inflationary pressures and periodic currency fluctuations in India — relevant given imported technology products and foreign subsidiaries.
risks.risk: Inflation and currency volatility in the Indian operating environment

risks.note: The pace of technological change is prompting increased regulatory attention, and evolving data localization requirements, digital sovereignty emphasis and sovereign cloud frameworks are reshaping how solutions must be architected and delivered — an opportunity, but also a compliance constraint on deployments.
risks.risk: Rising regulatory attention on AI, data localization and digital sovereignty

risks.note: As technology environments become distributed and interconnected, enterprises face growing complexity across architecture, security, governance and lifecycle management; the Company's value proposition rests on validating interoperability across multiple OEMs, so execution or integration failure directly affects customer outcomes and repeat business.
risks.risk: Complexity and execution risk in multi-OEM enterprise environments
